index 0000000000..fdb85e7572
--- /dev/null
+++ b/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RepresentableByTerminal.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
+-/
+import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
+import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.IsTerminal
+import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Comma.Over.Basic
+
+/-!
+# A presheaf with unique values is represented by the terminal object
+
+This file supplies the categorical bridge that was missing between "a presheaf
+`F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` has exactly one element at every test object" and
+"`F` is representable by the terminal object of `C`".
+
+Mathlib `v4.31` has `CategoryTheory.Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique` (a `C`-object
+`X` with `Unique (Y ⟶ X)` for every `Y` is terminal) and
+`CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal.ofUnique`, but **not** the presheaf-side
+statement: from `Nonempty (F.obj T)` and `Subsingleton (F.obj T)` at every `T`,
+build the natural bijection `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` that
+`Functor.RepresentableBy` is. Both sides of that bijection are singletons —
+the left because `Y` is terminal, the right by hypothesis — so the bijection
+and its naturality are `Subsingleton.elim`. Verified absent by search over
+mathlib and both projects; the nearest hits (`hasTerminal_of_unique`,
+`isTerminalEquivUnique`) are about representing objects, not represented
+presheaves.
+
+## Why it is worth a named declaration
+
+`Functor.RepresentableBy` is *data* (a chosen `Equiv` per object, plus a
+naturality equation), not a `Prop`. So even when a presheaf is manifestly a
+subterminal-and-inhabited functor, producing the `RepresentableBy` witness
+still requires building that `Equiv` by hand at every use site. This file does
+it once, at full categorical generality, so a consumer that has proved
+`Nonempty` and `Subsingleton` pointwise gets the representability witness by a
+single application — no `Equiv` plumbing.
+
+## The intended consumer
+
+`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` proves `Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))`
+for every `π` and test `T` (`DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero`, the empty
+divisor). If a lane proves the matching
+`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — that the empty divisor is the
+*only* relative effective divisor of degree `0` — then
+`representableByTerminal` yields
+`(DivFunctorDeg π 0).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (𝟙 S))` immediately, the first
+genuine `RepresentableBy` producer on the AJC divisor side. That `Subsingleton`
+is real content (a fact about `fiberDeg`, a `finrank` with a junk value at
+infinite dimension), and it is **not** discharged here; this file supplies only
+the categorical interface it plugs into.
+
+Everything here is about an arbitrary category and carries no algebraic-geometry
+hypothesis; nothing closes any `sorry`.
+-/
+
+universe v u
+
+namespace CategoryTheory.Functor
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
+
+/-- **A presheaf that is pointwise nonempty and subsingleton is represented by
+any terminal object.**
+
+The representing map `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` sends every morphism to the
+unique element of `F.obj (op X)` and back to the unique morphism `X ⟶ Y` (which
+exists because `Y` is terminal). Both round trips, and the naturality square,
+are forced by the two `Subsingleton`s.
+
+This is the presheaf-side companion of `Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique`, which is
+absent from mathlib `v4.31`. -/
+noncomputable def representableByTerminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
+    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
+    F.RepresentableBy Y where
+  homEquiv {X} := by
+    haveI := hne (Opposite.op X)
+    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
+    exact
+      { toFun := fun _ => Classical.arbitrary _
+        invFun := fun _ => hY.from X
+        left_inv := fun _ => hY.hom_ext _ _
+        right_inv := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _ }
+  homEquiv_comp {X X'} f g := by
+    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
+    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
+
+/-- **The `Unique`-packaged form of `representableByTerminal`.** When the values
+of `F` are literally `Unique` (a single default plus subsingleton), the same
+terminal object represents it. -/
+noncomputable def representableByTerminal_of_unique (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y) (h : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Unique (F.obj T)) :
+    F.RepresentableBy Y :=
+  representableByTerminal F hY (fun T => ⟨(h T).default⟩) (fun T => (h T).instSubsingleton)
+
+/-- **Existence corollary**: a pointwise nonempty-and-subsingleton presheaf is
+representable (forgets the chosen terminal object). -/
+theorem isRepresentable_of_terminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
+    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
+    F.IsRepresentable :=
+  (representableByTerminal F hY hne hss).isRepresentable
+
+end CategoryTheory.Functor

index 0000000000..e43e5c0e90
--- /dev/null
+++ b/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicEtUnitFieldComparison.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,177 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
+-/
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityClose
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtUnit
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.AbelElement
+
+/-!
+# The field-point comparison of the unit, LIFTED to the sheafified functor `picEt`
+
+The (C1)/(C2) campaign is stated on the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff`:
+
+* (C1) `PicEtAff.unit_injective` (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`, Kleiman 2.5(1)) —
+  étale separatedness, unconditional on every affine test algebra;
+* (C2) `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`, Kleiman
+  2.5(2)) — effectivity over a section-admitting field test;
+* their combination `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` — `relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`.
+
+But every *representability consumer* meets the honest relative Picard functor through
+`picEt` / `relPicFunctor`, not through `PicEtAff`: the degree-zero functor `pic0Functor`
+is a subfunctor of `picEtFunctor`, and the DAT-glue → `K_s` assembly (I-0248,
+`Picard/PicRepDatum.lean`) needs a representation of the sheafified functor at a
+separably closed / section-admitting field.  The comparison `PicEtAff.unit` and the
+functor-level unit `relPicToPicEt` are joined by `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
+(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`): on an affine test, evaluation at the terminal open
+`picEtAffineEquiv` collapses `relPicToPicEt` to `PicEtAff.unit`.  This file carries the
+campaign's two theorems across that collapse.
+
+## Honest scope
+
+Mathematically this is a **conjugation** of the landed `PicEtAff` results by the affine
+comparison isomorphism `picEtAffineEquiv`, so it introduces **no new mathematical
+content** and **no new hypothesis** — the field-point equivalence carries exactly the
+curve-point hypothesis `σ` of `EffectivityClose`.  It is worth landing because the
+composed statement at the level of the functor the representability headline names was
+recorded nowhere, and it is the interface between the C1/C2 campaign (output on
+`PicEtAff`) and the `RepresentableBy` route (input on `picEt`/`pic0`).
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicToPicEt_injective` — (C1) at the functor level: the unit
+  component `relPicToPicEt` is injective at **every** affine test, unconditionally.
+* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section` — the functor-level unit is a group
+  **isomorphism** `relPic C (Spec K) ≃* picEt C (Spec K)` over a section-admitting field
+  test, with `relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section_apply` identifying its map with
+  `relPicToPicEt`.
+* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicToPicEt_bijective_of_section` /
+  `relPicToPicEt_surjective_of_section` — the bijectivity/surjectivity corollaries in the
+  `Function.` idiom consumers cite.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory Opposite
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## (C1) at the functor level: injectivity of `relPicToPicEt` -/
+
+section injective
+
+variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
+
+omit [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
+/-- **`relPicToPicEt` factors through `PicEtAff.unit` by the affine comparison**: on an
+affine test its value is the affine comparison's inverse applied to the plus-construction
+unit.  The transported form of `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`. -/
+theorem relPicToPicEt_apply_eq_symm_unit (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
+    (z : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
+    relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z
+      = (picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm (PicEtAff.unit C A z) := by
+  rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A z, MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
+
+/-- **(C1) étale separatedness, functor level**: the unit component `relPicToPicEt` is
+injective on **every** affine test — unconditional, exactly as `PicEtAff.unit_injective`
+is.  It is the affine comparison composed with the injective plus-construction unit. -/
+theorem relPicToPicEt_injective (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
+    Function.Injective (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A)) := fun x y h => by
+  apply PicEtAff.unit_injective C A
+  rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A x, ← picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A y, h]
+
+end injective
+
+/-! ## (C1)+(C2) at the functor level: the field-point isomorphism -/
+
+section field
+
+variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
+variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
+
+/-- **The functor-level unit is a group isomorphism over a section-admitting field test**
+(Kleiman 2.5, both parts, at the level of the sheafified functor): if the curve admits a
+`K`-point `σ`, the unit component `relPicToPicEt C (Spec K)` is a `MulEquiv`
+`relPic C (Spec K) ≃* picEt C (Spec K)`.
+
+It is `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` conjugated by the affine comparison
+`picEtAffineEquiv`; `relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section_apply` records that its underlying map
+is `relPicToPicEt`, so nothing about the honest unit is lost in the packaging. -/
+noncomputable def relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
+    relPic C (overSpec k K) ≃* picEt C (overSpec k K) :=
+  (PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section C K σ).trans (picEtAffineEquiv C K).symm
+
+/-- The field-point isomorphism's underlying map is the functor-level unit
+`relPicToPicEt` — so it is the honest unit made bijective, not a different arrow. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section_apply (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C)
+    (z : relPic C (overSpec k K)) :
+    relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section C K σ z = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K) z := by
+  change (picEtAffineEquiv C K).symm (PicEtAff.unit C K z) = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K) z
+  rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C K z, MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
+
+/-- **(C1)+(C2) bijectivity, functor level**: over a section-admitting field test the unit
+component `relPicToPicEt` is bijective. -/
+theorem relPicToPicEt_bijective_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
+    Function.Bijective (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K)) := by
+  have h : ⇑(relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K))
+      = ⇑(relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section C K σ) :=
+    funext fun z => (relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section_apply C K σ z).symm
+  rw [h]
+  exact (relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section C K σ).bijective
+
+/-- **(C2) surjectivity, functor level**: over a section-admitting field test every étale
+Picard class on `Spec K` comes from an honest relative Picard class. -/
+theorem relPicToPicEt_surjective_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
+    Function.Surjective (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K)) :=
+  (relPicToPicEt_bijective_of_section C K σ).2
+
+end field
+
+/-! ## The degree of the unit image at the tautological field point
+
+`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)` is cut out of `picEt C (overSpec k K)` by the vanishing of
+`degAt` at every field point of `overSpec k K`.  The unit image `relPicToPicEt z` reads its
+degree at the *tautological* field point — the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)` — off the
+relative degree `relPicDeg K z` of `z` itself.  This is the identity-point instance of
+`AbelElement.degAt_relPicToPicEt`, isolated because it is the single instantiation the
+field-test arguments (`Pic0VanishingFieldTest`) consult in the vanishing direction. -/
+
+section degree
+
+variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
+variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
+  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
+
+/-- **The unit image's degree at the tautological point is the relative degree**: for
+`z : relPic C (overSpec k K)`, the degree of `relPicToPicEt z` at the identity field point
+`𝟙 (overSpec k K)` is `relPicDeg K z`.  The `degAt`-at-identity collapses by `picEtMap_id`
+and `AbelElement.degAt_relPicToPicEt`'s route (`picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`,
+`PicEtAff.degAff_unit`). -/
+theorem degAt_relPicToPicEt_id (z : relPic C (overSpec k K)) :
+    degAt (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K) z) (𝟙 (overSpec k K)) = relPicDeg K z := by
+  rw [degAt_relPicToPicEt (C := C) z (𝟙 (overSpec k K)), relPicMap_id]
+
+/-- **A unit image lands in `pic0Subgroup` only if the source has relative degree zero**:
+membership of `relPicToPicEt z` in the degree-zero subgroup forces `relPicDeg K z = 0`, by
+testing at the tautological point.  (The converse needs degree vanishing at *every* field
+point, which is genuinely stronger than degree zero over `K` alone — hence stated in this
+one honest direction.) -/
+theorem relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_pic0Subgroup {z : relPic C (overSpec k K)}
+    (hz : relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K) z ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) :
+    relPicDeg K z = 0 := by
+  have h := (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hz) K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
+  rwa [degAt_relPicToPicEt_id] at h
+
+end degree
+
+end
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	/-!
    11	# The divisor-to-Grassmannian comparison
    12	
    13	This file begins campaign milestone D2': a divisor family is twisted by a fixed
    14	module on the curve, and the pullback--pushforward base-change map followed by
    15	the divisor quotient gives the canonical evaluation morphism used by the
    16	Grassmannian construction.
    17	
    18	The definitions in the first section are unconditional.  In particular,
    19	`DivFamily.grassmannianEval` exists before the Riemann--Roch argument proves it
    20	epimorphic.  Keeping the map separate from its eventual `Epi` proof prevents
    21	uniform generation from becoming an assumption in the definition of the
    22	comparison.
    23	
    24	The second section records two affine algebra bridges used to turn finite flat
    25	pushforwards into the rank-indexed local-freeness predicate expected by
    26	`Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient`.  They do not introduce a representability gate:
    27	their inputs are ordinary finite-presentation, finiteness, and projectivity
    28	properties with producers elsewhere in the Picard development.
    29	-/
    30	
    31	set_option autoImplicit false
    32	
    33	universe u
    34	
    35	open CategoryTheory Limits
    36	
    37	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    38	
    39	namespace Scheme
    40	
    41	namespace DivFamily
    42	
    43	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
    44	
    45	/-- The twist of the divisor structure sheaf by a module on the original
    46	family.  For the D2' embedding, `L` is the chosen sufficiently positive
    47	projective twist. -/
    48	noncomputable def twist (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    49	    (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
    50	  Modules.tensorObj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
    51	
    52	/-- Tensor the divisor quotient `O -> O_D` with the pulled-back twist. -/
    53	noncomputable def twistQuotientMap (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    54	    (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶ x.twist L :=
    55	  (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
    56	    Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
    57	      ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)
    58	
    59	/-- The canonical D2' evaluation morphism.
    60	
    61	It first base-changes `π_* L` from `S` to `T`, then pushes forward the twisted
    62	divisor quotient along `X_T -> T`.  Uniform Riemann--Roch will prove that this
    63	map is an epimorphism for a sufficiently positive `L`; no such conclusion is
    64	built into the definition. -/
    65	noncomputable def grassmannianEval (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    66	    (Modules.pullback T.hom).obj ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) ⟶
    67	      (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) :=
    68	  pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
    69	      (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
    70	    (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)
    71	
    72	/-- The evaluation map is epi as soon as its two displayed factors are epi.
    73	This keeps the base-change and divisor-quotient obligations separate, so a
    74	later uniform-generation proof can discharge only the factor it actually
    75	proves. -/
    76	theorem grassmannianEval_epi (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
    77	    (hbase : Epi (pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom
    78	      (pullback.snd π T.hom) (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L))
    79	    (hquot : Epi ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map
    80	      (x.twistQuotientMap L))) :
    81	    Epi (x.grassmannianEval L) := by
    82	  letI := hbase
    83	  letI := hquot
    84	  dsimp [grassmannianEval]
    85	  infer_instance
    86	
    87	/-- **The conditional D2' quotient datum.**  Once the evaluation map is an
    88	epimorphism and its target has constant locally-free rank `d`, it is exactly a
    89	rank-`d` locally free quotient of the pulled-back pushforward of `L`.
    90	
    91	The two arguments are deliberately explicit: the evaluation map is the
    92	uniform-generation obligation, while the locally-free target is the
    93	finite/projective/rank obligation.  This constructor packages those genuine
    94	outputs without introducing a class or an instance that could hide either one.
    95	-/
    96	noncomputable def grassmannianQuotient (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
    97	    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
    98	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
    99	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   100	    LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T := by
   101	  letI := hEpi
   102	  exact {
   103	    F := (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)
   104	    q := x.grassmannianEval L
   105	    epi := inferInstance
   106	    locFree := hLocFree }
   107	
   108	/-- The quotient-class value of the D2' comparison in the relative
   109	Grassmannian functor.  This is the representation-facing object consumed by
   110	the Grassmannian representability theorem; well-definedness under
   111	`DivFamily.Rel` is a separate comparison lemma. -/
   112	noncomputable def grassmannianClass (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
   113	    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
   114	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   115	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   116	    (Grassmannian ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
   117	  Quotient.mk _ (grassmannianQuotient L x hEpi hLocFree)
   118	
   119	/-- The componentwise form of `grassmannianClass`: once the base-change and
   120	divisor-quotient factors are epi, only the target's rank condition remains. -/
   121	noncomputable def grassmannianClassOfComponents (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
   122	    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ}
   123	    (hbase : Epi (pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom
   124	      (pullback.snd π T.hom) (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L))
   125	    (hquot : Epi ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map
   126	      (x.twistQuotientMap L)))
   127	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   128	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   129	    (Grassmannian ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
   130	  grassmannianClass L x (grassmannianEval_epi L x hbase hquot) hLocFree
   131	
   132	end DivFamily

   137	/-- A finite global presentation of a module sheaf on `Spec R` induces a
   138	finite presentation of its module of global sections.
   139	
   140	The proof reconstructs the finite module cokernel underlying the sheaf
   141	presentation.  Full faithfulness of `tilde` identifies that cokernel with the
   142	global-section module, without any noetherian hypothesis on `R`. -/
   143	theorem module_finitePresentation_top_of_presentation
   144	    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) (P : M.Presentation)
   145	    [P.IsFinite] :
   146	    Module.FinitePresentation R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := by
   147	  let g := (tilde.functor R).preimage <|
   148	    (tildeFinsupp _).hom ≫ P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _ ≫ (tildeFinsupp _).inv
   149	  let Q := (P.generators.I →₀ R) ⧸ LinearMap.range g.hom
   150	  have hQ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q := by
   151	    apply Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective
   152	      (Submodule.mkQ (LinearMap.range g.hom)) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
   153	    rw [Submodule.ker_mkQ]
   154	    simpa only [LinearMap.range_eq_map] using Module.Finite.fg_top.map g.hom
   155	  let iso : cokernel ((tilde.functor R).map g) ≅
   156	      cokernel (P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _) := by
   157	    refine cokernel.mapIso _ _ (tildeFinsupp _) (tildeFinsupp _) ?_
   158	    simp only [g, (tilde.functor R).map_preimage]
   159	    simp
   160	  let eC : tilde (cokernel g) ≅ M :=
   161	    PreservesCokernel.iso (tilde.functor R) g ≪≫ iso ≪≫
   162	      IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso (colimit.isColimit _) P.isColimit
   163	  let eQ : tilde (ModuleCat.of R Q) ≅ M :=
   164	    (tilde.functor R).mapIso (ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient g).symm ≪≫ eC
   165	  haveI : IsIso M.fromTildeΓ := isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_presentation M P
   166	  let eΓ : ModuleCat.of R Q ≅ moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj M :=
   167	    (tilde.functor R).preimageIso (eQ ≪≫ qcoh_iso_tilde_sections M)
   168	  exact eΓ.toLinearEquiv.finitePresentation_iff.mp hQ

   173	theorem isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_finite_projective_sections
   174	    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent]
   175	    (hfin : Module.Finite R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)))
   176	    (hproj : Module.Projective R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)))
   177	    {d : ℕ} (hrank : ∀ t : PrimeSpectrum R, sectionsRankAtStalk M t = d) :

   181	  refine ⟨PrimeSpectrum R, U, ?_, fun t => ?_⟩
   182	  · rw [eq_top_iff]

1	\chapter{FGA representability of the Picard scheme}
     2	\label{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}
     3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforwardInstance.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Topology.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/GaloisDescent/SemilinearAlgebras.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/StableAffineCover.lean
     4	
     5	\section{Setup and motivation}
     6	\label{sec:fga_pic_setup}
     7	
     8	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
     9	integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
    10	Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
    11	\cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
    12	set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
    13	\'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
    14	\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
    15	representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
    16	packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.
    17	
    18	\medskip
    19	
    20	\textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
    21	constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
    22	different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.
    23	
    24	The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
    25	Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
    26	as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
    27	relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
    28	(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
    29	Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
    30	\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
    31	relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. It is the route of
    32	the proof written out under \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} below.
    33	
    34	That attribution needs one qualification, or the reader takes the chapter's headline
    35	theorem for a construction it is not. Neither route is carried out in full here:
    36	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} is a statement \emph{about} the existence predicate
    37	of \cref{def:has_pic_scheme}, from which it extracts the representing property, and the
    38	one assertion of this chapter that is not proved is
    39	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability_etale} --- a bare \texttt{sorry} in Lean, from which
    40	the \(\Pic^\sharp\)-shaped predicate \cref{def:inst_has_pic_scheme} is
    41	\emph{derived} rather than assumed. \Cref{rem:representability_is_conditional} states this
    42	precisely.
    43	So "the route of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}" names the argument its proof
    44	records, not a discharge of the predicate --- and the choice of route below is a choice
    45	about which argument is being built out, not about which theorem is available today.
    46	
    47	The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
    48	separably closed field, from the open loci
    49	\[
    50	  C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
    51	\]
    52	cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
    53	points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
    54	before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
    55	pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
    56	classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme. Its structure, and the parts of it that
    57	are established, are the subject of \cref{sec:fga_pic_milne_kollar}.

   101	(\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section

   104	base change), then the comparison maps

   419	  Let \(\alpha : Z \to P\) be a morphism of \'etale sheaves on \((\Sch/k)\).
   420	  Set \(R := Z \times_P Z\). Suppose:
   421	  \begin{enumerate}
   422	    \item \(\alpha\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves;
   423	    \item \(Z\) is representable by a quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme;
   424	    \item \(R\) is representable by a \(k\)-scheme;
   425	    \item the first projection \(R \to Z\) is representable by a smooth
   426	      and proper map.
   427	  \end{enumerate}
   428	  Then \(P\) is representable by a quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme, and \(\alpha\)
   429	  is representable by a smooth map.

   431	
   432	\begin{proof}
   433	  By (ii) the structure map \(Z \to \Spec k\) is quasi-projective, hence
   434	  separated, so the first projection \(Z \times_k Z \to Z\) is separated.
   435	  By (iv) the first projection \(R \to Z\) is proper; it factors through
   436	  \(h : R \to Z \times_k Z\) over the diagonal embedding (the second
   437	  component is the second projection of \(R \to Z \times_P Z\)). The map
   438	  \(h\) is therefore proper, and a monomorphism (because \(R\) is the graph
   439	  of an equivalence relation on \(Z\), hence injective on \(T\)-points).
   440	  By EGA IV 8.11.5, a proper monomorphism is a closed immersion: \(h\) is a
   441	  closed embedding.
   442	
   443	  Hence \(R \hookrightarrow Z \times_k Z\) is a flat (by (iv)) and proper
   444	  equivalence relation on the quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Z\). By the
   445	  theory of flat-and-proper effective equivalence relations on
   446	  quasi-projective schemes (Altman--Kleiman; the construction places
   447	  the graph \(R \subseteq Z \times_k Z\) inside the universal subscheme of
   448	  the Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{Z/k}\) and descends to a closed subscheme
   449	  \(Q \subseteq \Hilb_{Z/k}\) representing the quotient), there exist a
   450	  quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Q\) and a faithfully flat, projective map
   451	  \(Z \to Q\) with \(R = Z \times_Q Z\).
   452	
   453	  The map \(Z \to Q\) is flat and proper; its fibers, up to field
   454	  extension, coincide with those of \(R \to Z\), which are smooth by
   455	  hypothesis. Hence \(Z \to Q\) is smooth.
   456	
   457	  Finally, \(Z \to Q\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves (an \'etale
   458	  cover of any \(T\)-point of \(Q\) pulls back to a \(T'\)-point of \(Z\), by
   459	  EGA IV 17.16.3 (ii) applied to \(Z \times_Q T \to T\)). In the category
   460	  of \'etale sheaves, both \(Q\) and \(P\) are coequalisers of the pair
   461	  \(R \rightrightarrows Z\); the coequaliser is unique up to unique
   462	  isomorphism, so \(Q\) represents \(P\). Smoothness of \(\alpha : Z \to P\)
   463	  is the smoothness of \(Z \to Q\) just shown.
   464	\end{proof}

  2383	Therefore, $h$ is a closed embedding by \cite[8.11.5]{EGAIV3}.
  2384	
  2385	Plainly, for each $S$-scheme $T$, the subset $R(T)\subset
  2386	Z(T)\x_{S(T)}Z(T)$ is the graph of an equivalence relation.  Also, the
  2387	map of schemes $R\to Z$ is flat and proper, and $Z$ is a
  2388	quasi-projective $S$-scheme.  It follows that there exist a
  2389	quasi-projective $S$-scheme $Q$ and a faithfully flat and projective map
  2390	$Z\to Q$ such that $R=Z\x_QZ$.  (In other words, a flat and proper
  2391	equivalence relation on a quasi-projective scheme is effective.)  In
  2392	fact, $R$ defines a map from $Z$ to the Hilbert scheme $\IHilb_{Z/S}$, and
  2393	its graph lies in the universal scheme as a closed subscheme, which
  2394	descends to $Q\subset \IHilb_{Z/S}$; for more details, see \cite[Thm.~(2.9),
  2395	p.~70]{AK80}.

  1370	\subsection{The relative-divisor input}
  1371	\label{subsec:sorry_has_div_functor}
  1372	
  1373	The relative-divisor functor \(\Div_{X/S}\) of
  1374	\cref{def:div_functor} is the subfunctor of the Hilbert functor
  1375	\(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of relative effective Cartier
  1376	divisors, in the invertible-kernel quotient encoding of
  1377	\cref{def:div_family}. The presheaf \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of

  1386	\label{subsec:sorry_has_abel_map}
  1387	
  1388	The class \cref{def:has_abel_map} carries the natural transformation whose
  1389	value on a divisor family is

  1395	comparison isomorphism) with the group-presheaf negation

  1402	\label{subsec:fga_pic_closure_order_summary}

  1404	The FGA construction consumes the relative-divisor functor and Abel map,

  1412	\section{Related constructions}
  1413	\label{sec:fga_pic_out_of_scope}
  1414	
  1415	The representable Picard scheme and its group structure interact with the
  1416	following constructions, treated in the indicated companion chapters.
  1417	\begin{itemize}
  1418	  \item \textbf{Identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\)} --- the open and
  1419	    closed subgroup scheme of \(\Pic_{C/k}\) containing the unit and
  1420	    consisting of those classes lying in the connected component of
  1421	    \(\Pic_{C/k}\). Its dimension, smoothness, and abelian-variety
  1422	    structure are treated in \cref{chap:Picard_IdentityComponent} and
  1423	    \cref{chap:Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety}.
  1424	  \item \textbf{Quot scheme representability} --- consumed by
  1425	    \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} via \texttt{thm:quot\_representable}
  1426	    (\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}), not re-proved here. It is an input of the
  1427	    quotient route only; the Milne--Koll\'ar route of
  1428	    \cref{sec:fga_pic_milne_kollar} does not use it, although it does use the
  1429	    Grassmannian and flattening substrate of the same chapters.
  1430	  \item \textbf{\'Etale sheafification.} The relative Picard presheaf and its
  1431	    topology-parametric sheafification are constructed in
  1432	    \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. Under the
  1433	    standing rational-point hypothesis, Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 identifies
  1434	    the plain relative functor with the \'etale sheafification.
  1435	  \item \textbf{Universal Poincar\'e sheaf} (Kleiman~\S 4, Ex.~4.3)
  1436	    --- exists when \(\Pic_{C/k}\) represents \(\Pic_{C/k}\) itself and
  1437	    \(C/k\) has a section. Under the chapter's standing rational-point
  1438	    hypothesis both conditions in fact hold (Thm.~2.5 identifies the
  1439	    plain functor with the represented sheaf), so the Poincar\'e sheaf
  1440	    is then available as an associated construction.
  1441	  \item \textbf{Mumford's example} (Kleiman~\S 4, Eg.~4.14), counter-examples
  1442	    to representability for non-integral geometric fibers --- not
  1443	    relevant to a smooth proper geometrically integral curve.
  1444	\end{itemize}

+/-!
+# A presheaf with unique values is represented by the terminal object
+
+This file supplies the categorical bridge that was missing between "a presheaf
+`F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` has exactly one element at every test object" and
+"`F` is representable by the terminal object of `C`".
+
+Mathlib `v4.31` has `CategoryTheory.Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique` (a `C`-object
+`X` with `Unique (Y ⟶ X)` for every `Y` is terminal) and
+`CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal.ofUnique`, but **not** the presheaf-side
+statement: from `Nonempty (F.obj T)` and `Subsingleton (F.obj T)` at every `T`,
+build the natural bijection `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` that
+`Functor.RepresentableBy` is. Both sides of that bijection are singletons —
+the left because `Y` is terminal, the right by hypothesis — so the bijection
+and its naturality are `Subsingleton.elim`. Verified absent by search over
+mathlib and both projects; the nearest hits (`hasTerminal_of_unique`,
+`isTerminalEquivUnique`) are about representing objects, not represented
+presheaves.
+
+## Why it is worth a named declaration
+
+`Functor.RepresentableBy` is *data* (a chosen `Equiv` per object, plus a
+naturality equation), not a `Prop`. So even when a presheaf is manifestly a
+subterminal-and-inhabited functor, producing the `RepresentableBy` witness
+still requires building that `Equiv` by hand at every use site. This file does
+it once, at full categorical generality, so a consumer that has proved
+`Nonempty` and `Subsingleton` pointwise gets the representability witness by a
+single application — no `Equiv` plumbing.
+
+## The intended consumer
+
+`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` proves `Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))`
+for every `π` and test `T` (`DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero`, the empty
+divisor). If a lane proves the matching
+`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — that the empty divisor is the
+*only* relative effective divisor of degree `0` — then
+`representableByTerminal` yields
+`(DivFunctorDeg π 0).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (𝟙 S))` immediately, the first
+genuine `RepresentableBy` producer on the AJC divisor side. That `Subsingleton`
+is real content (a fact about `fiberDeg`, a `finrank` with a junk value at
+infinite dimension), and it is **not** discharged here; this file supplies only
+the categorical interface it plugs into.
+
+Everything here is about an arbitrary category and carries no algebraic-geometry
+hypothesis; nothing closes any `sorry`.
+-/
+
+universe w v u
+
+namespace CategoryTheory.Functor
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
+
+/-- **A presheaf that is pointwise nonempty and subsingleton is represented by
+any terminal object.**
+
+The representing map `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` sends every morphism to the
+unique element of `F.obj (op X)` and back to the unique morphism `X ⟶ Y` (which
+exists because `Y` is terminal). Both round trips, and the naturality square,
+are forced by the two `Subsingleton`s.
+
+This is the presheaf-side companion of `Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique`, which is
+absent from mathlib `v4.31`. -/
+noncomputable def representableByTerminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
+    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
+    F.RepresentableBy Y where
+  homEquiv {X} := by
+    haveI := hne (Opposite.op X)
+    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
+    exact
+      { toFun := fun _ => Classical.arbitrary _
+        invFun := fun _ => hY.from X
+        left_inv := fun _ => hY.hom_ext _ _
+        right_inv := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _ }
+  homEquiv_comp {X X'} f g := by
+    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
+    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
+
+/-- **The `Unique`-packaged form of `representableByTerminal`.** When the values
+of `F` are literally `Unique` (a single default plus subsingleton), the same
+terminal object represents it. -/
+noncomputable def representableByTerminal_of_unique (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y) (h : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Unique (F.obj T)) :
+    F.RepresentableBy Y :=
+  representableByTerminal F hY (fun T => ⟨(h T).default⟩) (fun T => (h T).instSubsingleton)
+
+/-- **Existence corollary**: a pointwise nonempty-and-subsingleton presheaf is
+representable (forgets the chosen terminal object). -/
+theorem isRepresentable_of_terminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
+    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
+    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
+    F.IsRepresentable :=
+  (representableByTerminal F hY hne hss).isRepresentable
+
+end CategoryTheory.Functor

title: 'Div-zero: the first DivFamily producer, and Div^0 representable by the terminal
  object'

summary: 'ADVANCED, NOT CLOSED, by pic-e (run 0095). Owner released. Scheme.DivFamily
  HAS AN INHABITANT; the seam sorry fgaPicardRepresentability is untouched and NO
  antecedent of it is witnessed for any curve.


  LANDED, DO NOT REDO. Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean + Picard/DivFamilyZeroAbel.lean,
  both rooted at AlgebraicJacobian.lean. 34 declarations across the two files, ZERO
  code sorries, ALL 34 axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] against
  fgaPicardRepresentability firing sorryAx in the same probe with oleans rebuilt FIRST.
  Verified independently by a fresh-context audit which found four defects, all accepted
  and fixed (see below).


  * DivFamily.zero pi T -- the EMPTY DIVISOR, for ARBITRARY pi : X -> S and T : Over
  S. F = 0, q = 0, so ker q = O_{X_T} and the divisor condition holds because O/O
  = 0 cuts out D = empty. No hypothesis on pi: not proper, not smooth, not separated.
  THE FIRST INHABITANT: at the parent commit, 148 mentions of DivFamily in AJC and
  zero producers (audited independently; both numbers exactly confirmed).

  * WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS, measured not asserted: IsLocallyTrivial (0 : Y.Modules)
  is FALSE at every point (restrict-of-zero is zero, forcing subsingleton sections,
  contra Scheme.component_nontrivial). So kerLocallyTrivial at F = 0 asserts a rank-ONE
  statement and genuinely excludes the rival ''unit divisor'' F = O, q = id.

  * Base change: pullbackAlong_zero, so DivFunctor.map_zeroClass makes zeroClass a
  GLOBAL SECTION of Div, not a per-object choice. fiberDeg_zero / hasFiberDeg_zero
  give degree 0 everywhere, hence an inhabitant of (DivFunctorDeg pi 0).obj T.

  * PicScheme.abelMap_zero: A([empty]) = 0, Kleiman''s O(empty) = O normalisation
  and the FIRST COMPUTED VALUE of abelMap in the project (audited: no prior declaration
  evaluates abelMap/abelDeg/abelMapWitness at a closed term). abelDeg_zero is the
  same through the degree-refined map. Stated at abelMapWitness''s instance with no
  [HasAbelMap C] binder, so the trivial constant-zero inhabitant cannot satisfy it.

  * REUSABLE BRICKS ABSENT FROM MATHLIB (audited against mathlib + both projects):
  Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_isZero (a zero sheaf of modules is finitely presented
  -- not synthesizable), Modules.coversTop_singleton_top, Modules.preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor
  (proved; instance search fails at 1.6M heartbeats), Modules.isZero_free_pempty.


  WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and it is the row''s remaining content. Div^0 is NOT represented
  by the terminal object: this file proves the Nonempty half only. The missing half
  is Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg pi 0).obj T) -- that the empty divisor is the ONLY
  degree-0 one. AUDIT-CONFIRMED that Nonempty + Subsingleton at every T SUFFICES,
  with naturality free (homEquiv_comp closes by Subsingleton.elim). So this row is
  one Subsingleton away from a genuine RepresentableBy producer on the divisor side.


  DO NOT re-derive it from the sibling. AJCR has the analogous Subsingleton landed
  (instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero, and the general-ring form with a full RepresentableBy
  producer). It does NOT transport, and the reason is sharper than the carrier mismatch:
  their proof never passes through a finrank -- it runs on IsCertified and rankAtStalk
  over Away localisations of section rings. AJC''s fiberDeg IS a Module.finrank of
  fibre sections. Their success is also evidence against pricing this as a finiteness
  question at all.


  NOT DISCHARGED, stated because it is the natural over-reading: PicScheme.classDegree_ne_zero_of_exists_pos_fiberDeg
  (Picard/IdentityComponent.lean) needs a family of degree d != 0. The empty divisor
  has degree 0, so it is precisely the family that acceptance test cannot use. That
  producer needs a rational point and the positivity bridge pic-b is building.


  FOUR AUDIT FINDINGS AGAINST MY OWN WORK, all accepted: (1) Module.Flat.of_subsingleton''
  was REDUNDANT -- mathlib''s Module.Free.of_subsingleton is a priority-100 instance
  so the goal closes by inferInstance; my evidence had been an exact? failure, which
  does not run instance synthesis. Deleted. (2) Three citations named the FILE not
  the NAMESPACE and all three failed #check; fixed, and all 13 cited names are now
  #check-verified. (3) ''properSupport is a real hypothesis for a nonempty divisor''
  was never measured; dropped. (4) ''no lane holds the Subsingleton'' was FALSE.'

summary: 'STATUS AND ANCHOR CORRECTED by review-ajc 2026-07-29. This node was `done`
  and cited a deliverable that does not exist; both were wrong.


  WHAT THIS NODE DISCHARGES, repointed. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`
  — a bare `sorry`, the project''s central open obligation. The previous text said
  "Discharges instHasPicScheme (FGAPicRepresentability.lean:259)". Both halves were
  stale: `instHasPicScheme` exists in no `.lean` file (deleted 2026-07-28 under I-0491,
  never discharged; every grep hit is prose — re-verified at HEAD 2026-07-30, 26 hits,
  all docstring or comment), and line 259 fell mid-docstring, inside the bundling
  rationale above `class HasPicScheme`. The live gate is `HasPicSchemeEt`, whose instance
  `instHasPicSchemeEt` is `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1` — a projection of that
  same sorry, so the gate synthesizes freely and carries the sorry into every consumer.


  AND THE REPOINT ITSELF WENT STALE, in the paragraph announcing it (review-ajc r7,
  2026-07-30). The four numbers above — 347 for the theorem, 355 for the class, 366
  for the instance, 263 for `class HasPicScheme` — were all wrong at HEAD nine hours
  later: the theorem head is 757, the sorry 765, and every one of 347/355/366 lands
  mid-docstring, i.e. the SAME defect this row was corrected for. They are now removed
  rather than refreshed. Cite declaration names here; do not restore line numbers.
  This is the fifth repetition of a failure this lane has filed four times, and the
  third time the repair re-created it.


  THE ASSEMBLY STEP, unchanged in substance. Glue the `h0=1` loci into `Pic^r` over
  a separably closed field (campaign J1-J5; needs the mathlib 01JJ engine and a universe
  bridge, since `picSharp` is `Type (u+1)`-valued while 01JJ wants `Type u`), spread
  the finite glue datum to a finite Galois level (G1), descend `picSharp` points through
  rigidified pairs (G3), and assemble the degree pieces as a coproduct over Z (G4).


  WHY IT IS NOT CLOSE. Of the campaign modules this node consumes, `Picard/MilneGlue.lean`
  (J5), `Picard/PicSharpGaloisDescent.lean` (G3) and `Picard/PicTotalAssembly.lean`
  (G4) do not exist on disk, and neither do their inputs B1 `PicSharpZariskiSheaf`,
  B4 `PicSharpDegree`, B6 `PicSharpSeparatedDevice`, or the `Div^d` chain D2''-D4''.

  vocabulary at the pinned mathlib; protection I-0074 caveat 2), and must not be built
  against.

  docstring in place.

  CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER, as the conclusion of an implication whose antecedent is
  PointedPicSharpRep -- pointed picSharp-representability, uniform in the base field,
  bundled with FiniteInAffine of the representing scheme. So a lane proving that antecedent
  closes the project''s central sorry by exact. This row said the work is ''a ROUTE
  REPAIR, not a missing representability theorem''; that is now a theorem rather than
  an assessment.

  lanes, no row mentioning the other two. exists_finiteGalois_level_hasRationalPoint_of_geometricallyIntegral
  produces a finite GALOIS level with a point UNCONDITIONALLY from the seam''s own
  binders; picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport crosses to picEt with no section;
  seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree descends to k with hq and hcov discharged
  INTERNALLY.

  inputs the descent-assembly row lists are GONE: hcov (pic-f), the quotient via the
  GLOBAL instance hasGaloisQuotient_of_orbitsInAffineOpen with NO affineness, the
  G1 match (isInvariantMatch_canonical). The one remaining instance binder is OrbitsInAffineOpen,
  and orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine reduces THAT to a scheme-level property,
  so the antecedent need not name the Galois level. Price against seamClauseOne_of_hasGoodGaloisLevel:
  it needs ONE Galois level, NO rational point in its statement, and NOT [GeometricallyIntegral].

  the affine locus'' and ''inferInstance at an abstract action carrying the orbit
  hypothesis but not affineness FAILS'' are STALE -- inferInstance SUCCEEDS there

  discharges the instance. Not edited in that file.

  is unproved in-tree -- it IS the Milne-Kollar campaign''s output; (b) no curve is
  exhibited with FiniteInAffine at its Picard scheme, and that needs real quasi-projectivity,
  which mathlib v4.31 lacks at this pin (exact? fails at an arbitrary scheme AND at
  a LocallyOfFiniteType separated one).

  up to FiniteInAffine -- picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint gives three of four conjuncts,
  measured, reports sorryAx. So AXIOM-CHECK any claimed proof; on this seam provability
  is not a discriminating control.

  now landed as nonempty_representableBy_picSharp_of_isIso, and clause (2) supplies

  the gap is only at pointless ones. (2) IsSeparated was a conjunct of my antecedent

  relocating item 3''s stale sentence to a shape it does not describe. (4) ''FiniteInAffine
  cannot be stated outside the antecedent'' -- refuted by two declarations in the
  same file.'

244:{"kind": "tool_result", "at": "2026-07-31T07:57:59.515357+00:00", "text": "", "tool": "Bash", "data": {"content": "---\nname: horizon-inbox\ndescription: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.\n---\n\nThe inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and\nfuture), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files\nby hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or\nfields.\n\n## Read\n\n- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,\n  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters\n  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,\n  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,\n  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.\n- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not\n  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,\n  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an\n  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.\n- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for\n  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.\n- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is\n  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale\n  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because\n  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an\n  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.\n- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which\n  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for\n  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:\n  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids\n  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is\n  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.\n- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,\n  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /\n  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation\n  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.\n  Scope/project says what the item is about.\n- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed\n  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other\n  projects' and other teams' addressed items.\n- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The\n  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every\n  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:\n  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.\n- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),\n  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),\n  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the\n  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project\n  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),\n  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).\n\n## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)\n\nEach running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two\nlightweight overlays keep it navigable:\n\n- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or\n  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your\n  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);\n  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with\n  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own\n  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your\n  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.\n- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see\n  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read\n  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`\n  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:\n  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal\n  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.\n\nRead in this order before editing:\n\n1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every\n   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.\n2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each\n   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read\n   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.\n3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.\n\nThe reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass\nit explicitly.\n\n## Act\n\nAuthorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is\nattributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do\n**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the\n`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).\nIf you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent\nwork-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown\nnext to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and\ncomments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the\nUI); you do not pass this yourself.\n\nNew inbox items use a two-part body:\n\n- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row\n  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.\n- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,\n  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an\n  item that is only a title is rejected.\n\nWrite bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Operational\nmessages are deltas, not reports. Default to one sentence or at most three short\nbullets covering conclusion, new evidence, and next action; do not repeat the\nthread, commit diff, or session history. Use headings only when a genuinely\nmulti-part decision needs them. Agent comments target at most 600 characters and\nare rejected above 1200; descriptions/opening messages target 800 and are\nrejected above 2400. Humans are not subject to these bounds.\n\nDo not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or\n`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest\nof that paragraph concise.\n\nBefore opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using\n`horizon inbox list --status open --query \"key words\" --json` and, when relevant,\n`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not\nopen a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the\nmain description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already\nsolved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not\nobvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.\n\n### Conversation lifecycle\n\nA conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A\none-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.\n\n1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and\n   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query \"key words\"\n   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not\n   open one thread per incremental finding.\n2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the\n   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a\n   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.\n3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and\n   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same\n   team.\n4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own\n   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a\n   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then\n   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a\n   warning says the inbox is full.\n5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and\n   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave\n   it open for the human to consume/archive unless the human explicitly delegates\n   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is\n   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.\n6. **End-of-session sweep:** before the final report, inspect open conversations\n   in which your task is `started_by`. Archive every resolved one and state a real\n   blocker on any that must remain open. An accumulation of open conversations is\n   unfinished coordination, not harmless history.\n\n- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body \"...\"` — progress note on an item (record\n  what changed; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name\n  into the body; authorship is automatic. Comment only at a **key advance** such\n  as a milestone, ruled-out route, blocker, correction, or conclusion. Update the\n  existing thread with the delta instead of re-establishing its full context.\n- `horizon inbox dm task:<id> [task:<id> ...] --body \"Topic\\n\\nOpening message\"`\n  — start a one-to-one or group conversation. Use `horizon ps` to discover live\n  teams. Use it only after the lifecycle search above. The sender remains a\n  participant and owns closure; every reply makes the thread unread for the other\n  participants. Humans read and reply from the live dashboard.\n- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that\n  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming\n  the result and the idea — e.g. \"Proved $H^i(X,\\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\\dim X$ by\n  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology.\" Mention Lean declaration\n  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not\n  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:\n  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.\n- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but\n  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or\n  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the\n  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.\n  For a conversation you initiated, this is the normal \"discussion finished\"\n  operation after its answer/conclusion has been consumed.\n- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work\n  you genuinely concluded and want to keep visible outside the archive. Before\n  completing, add a short **conclusion comment**: first the mathematical\n  conclusion (what was proved/established, in words + LaTeX), then concise\n  metadata (runs, approximate LOC, files/declarations involved). A reader should\n  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.\n- `horizon inbox add --body \"Short title\\n\\nDescription with details and next action.\" [--to R] [--project P] [--persistent|--temporary] [--agent <name> if a subagent]`\n  — open a new item.\n  - `--to` is the recipient: `horizon`, `human`, `project:<name>`, or a direct\n    message to another team `task:<id>` / `run:<id>`.\n    Use `--to project:<name>` to message another project (e.g. \"I rewrote your\n    `foo` declaration more cleanly, you may want it\"); use `--to task:<id>` to\n    message a specific running team.\n  - `--owner <task-id>` / `--mine` keeps the item in one team's inbox instead of\n    the shared default.\n  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).\n  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`\n    tag to the body.\n  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,\n    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.\n- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body \"Short memory title\\n\\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end.\"` — record a durable\n  note / dead end. Memory lives in the inbox, so it is rendered in the \"Memory\"\n  section and a human can prune it like any other item.\n- `horizon inbox protect --body \"...\" [--project P] [--file F] [--declaration D] [--blueprint-node N]`\n  — add a semantic standing constraint the Horizon agent must respect (a soft freeze),\n  e.g. \"do not change the signature of `Foo.bar`\". These render as a\n  \"Protected\" section; honour them, including semantic ones. For a target that\n  must be mechanically blocked before dispatch, the user uses the config-backed\n  `horizon freeze add <file|declaration|blueprint-node> <target>` command instead.\n\nReading convention: an item tagged `[persistent]` is a standing rule — respect\nit every round and keep it open while relevant. `[temporary]` (or untagged) is\none-shot — archive it once consumed. Items in the \"Protected\" section are never\nmodified.\n", "exit_code": 0}, "usage": null}

## (A) Producers of `RepresentableBy` for `picEt` / `picSharp`: **none**

All four below I probed with `#print axioms`; all are `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

1. `AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.represents` — `Picard/GrassmannianQuot.lean:5608`. Sorry-free, clean. Mechanism: **explicit chart construction + glued-scheme universal property** — forward map pulls back the tautological rank quotient, inverse is `grPointOfRankQuotient` built chart-by-chart and glued.
2. `Scheme.Grassmannian.prodRepresentableBy` — `Picard/GrassmannianRepresentability.lean:357`. Clean. Mechanism: **adjunction/terminal-object argument** — `Over.forget S ⊣ Over.star S` transports absolute representability into `Over S` (this is the "representable by base change of the absolute object" route). Sorry-free (the whole file's project-import closure is 1 module), clean. Mechanism: **Zariski descent / open cover of the base** — a `Type 0` total-functor encoding fed to mathlib's `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` (Stacks 01JJ), then transported back to `Over S`.
4. `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism` — `Picard/IdentityComponent.lean:737`, via the private `identityComponentRepresentableBy:707`.
